extracted.intended_audience: patent prosecutors, patent attorneys/agents, and litigators drafting or evaluating software-related patents (US)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and evaluating Beauregard (computer-readable-medium) claims for software, with attention to USPTO/US case-law pitfalls (Alice, CyberSource, Nuijten) and prosecution/litigation strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directed to a tangible medium
rubrics_metrics.description: A Beauregard claim must be directed to a tangible medium (a computer-readable medium) rather than to abstract information alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beauregard claims typically recite a floppy disk or CD-ROM as the computer-readable medium and are thus sometimes called 'floppy disk' claims. Framing the claim as an article of manufacture (the medium) is the core formal requirement of the Beauregard format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contain program instructions or other software-related content
rubrics_metrics.description: The claimed medium must contain program instructions or other software-related content encoded on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft claims to explicitly recite that instructions, code, or software content are encoded on the medium so the claim is to the medium-with-instructions rather than to abstract information alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with 35 U.S.C. § 112 requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauregard claims must be written in a way that complies with 35 U.S.C. § 112 (written description, enablement, and definiteness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the claim language and the specification provide sufficient written description of the instructions and how they operate, enablement of the claimed invention, and definite claim scope to avoid §112 rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify 'non-transitory' computer-readable media to avoid signal-based rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should specify 'non-transitory' computer-readable media to avoid rejections based on signal or transitory embodiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including the term 'non-transitory' in the claim preamble or recitation (e.g., 'a non-transitory computer-readable medium') helps avoid Nuijten-style rejections that treat transitory signals as unpatentable subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underlying method or invention must be patent-eligible
rubrics_metrics.description: If the underlying method or inventive concept is not patent-eligible, recasting it as a Beauregard claim will not render it patent-eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-Alice jurisprudence (and cases like CyberSource) show that a Beauregard claim cannot salvage patent eligibility where the underlying method is an ineligible abstract idea; evaluate and draft method/system claims for eligibility in parallel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid claims that are mere manipulation or reorganization of data
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that merely recite manipulation or reorganization of data are likely to be held patent-ineligible under Alice/CyberSource principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on reciting data rearrangement or formatting; include technical improvements, inventive steps, or other aspects that demonstrate more than an abstract idea or mere data processing to strengthen eligibility arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim in multiple statutory categories as best practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Include claim sets across multiple statutory categories: method, system/apparatus, and computer-readable medium (Beauregard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing complementary claims in different statutory classes provides flexibility during prosecution and litigation; if one category encounters eligibility issues, others may remain viable for amendment or enforcement.
